Done for this planning turn. Summary:

**Changed:** Replaced the empty `strategy.py` with a signal-tiered "green water" strategy — since satellite chlorophyll (`ocean.chl`) is entirely null this dataset, it uses Scripps Pier water-temp trend + upwelling (CUTI) relaxation as proxies, confirmed by the fleet's recent pooled yellowtail-per-angler rate, to gate trip size (half day → 3/4-full day → overnight/1.5-day) and speculative 14-day-ahead PTO commits restricted to the historically productive Apr-Jun/Sep-Nov window with budget/PTO reserves held back for the fall. Wrote detailed `notes.md` with season-1 findings (Oct was the best month by far despite negative ONI, contradicting a warm-ONI thesis; spring/June secondary bumps; July was a dud despite heavy fleet effort) and open questions to check next turn. Posted one forum note sharing the ONI-surprise and the missing-chlorophyll-data finding.

**Why:** Day 1 of a fresh practice season with zero bookings yet — the priority was extracting what last year's full-season data actually says about timing (since chl data isn't available, had to find working proxies) and encoding a patient, signal-driven reflex strategy plus a clear plan for what to validate once season-2 data starts arriving.
